questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: General introduction and importance of biomolecules
questions.question: Nucleic acids such as DNA and RNA are polymers whose repeating monomer units are

solution.key_concept: Most biomolecules are polymers of simple units: monosaccharides form polysaccharides, amino acids form proteins and nucleotides form nucleic acids.
steps: Each polymer class has its own monomer.
Nucleic acids are built from nucleotides.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): nucleotides
solution.why_not_others: Amino acids are the monomers of proteins. Monosaccharides are the monomers of polysaccharides. Nucleosides lack the phosphate group, so they are not the repeating units of nucleic acids.
solution.common_trap: Confusing nucleoside (no phosphate) with nucleotide (has a phosphate).
solution.time_saving_tip: The monomer of a nucleic acid is a nucleotide.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: General introduction and importance of biomolecules
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of biomolecule and its function is correctly matched?
options: Hormones: storage and transmission of genetic information
Cellulose: structural material of plant cell walls
Vitamins: chief source of energy for the body
Nucleic acids: chemical messengers that coordinate body functions

solution.key_concept: Each class of biomolecule has a characteristic biological role.
steps: Carbohydrates supply energy and also act as structural material, for example cellulose in plant cell walls.
Nucleic acids carry heredity, hormones act as chemical messengers, and vitamins are needed in small amounts for growth and health.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Cellulose: structural material of plant cell walls
solution.why_not_others: Genetic information is stored by nucleic acids, not hormones. The chief energy source is carbohydrates, not vitamins. Chemical messengers are hormones, not nucleic acids.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the roles of hormones and nucleic acids.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: General introduction and importance of biomolecules
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Cellulose, a carbohydrate, serves as a structural material in plant cell walls.
statements.R: Carbohydrates cannot act as a source of energy in living systems.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Carbohydrates are the chief energy source and also provide structural support.
steps: Cellulose is the structural material of plant cell walls, so A is true.
Carbohydrates are the chief energy source of living systems, so R is false.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A is true but R is false
solution.why_not_others: R contradicts the main role of carbohydrates, so any option that treats R as true is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Assuming that a structural role rules out an energy role.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: General introduction and importance of biomolecules
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Polysaccharides, proteins and nucleic acids are polymers built from monosaccharides, amino acids and nucleotides respectively.
statements.II: Hormones act as chemical messengers that coordinate body functions, whereas vitamins are required in small amounts for normal growth and health.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Biopolymers are built from monomer units, and hormones and vitamins act as regulators.
steps: The monomer-polymer pairs in Statement I are all correct.
The roles of hormones and vitamins in Statement II are correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Neither statement contains an error, so every option that marks one of them incorrect is ruled out.
solution.common_trap: Suspecting a swapped order in Statement I when the order is actually right.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is a ketohexose?

solution.key_concept: Monosaccharides are named by the type of carbonyl group and the number of carbons.
steps: Fructose has six carbons and a keto group at C2, so it is a ketohexose.
Glucose is an aldohexose, ribose is an aldopentose and glyceraldehyde is an aldotriose.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Fructose
solution.why_not_others: Glucose, ribose and glyceraldehyde all contain an aldehyde group, so they are aldoses.
solution.common_trap: Calling glucose a ketose because it is a hexose like fructose.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following compounds fits the general formula $C_x(H_2O)_y$ but is NOT a carbohydrate?

solution.key_concept: $C_x(H_2O)_y$ is not a valid definition of carbohydrates.
steps: Acetic acid can be written as $C_2(H_2O)_2$, so it fits the formula, but it is not a carbohydrate.
Rhamnose is a carbohydrate that does not fit the formula.
Glucose and sucrose both fit the formula and are carbohydrates.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Acetic acid, $C_2H_4O_2$
solution.why_not_others: Rhamnose is the opposite exception: it is a carbohydrate but does not fit the formula. Glucose and sucrose are genuine carbohydrates.
solution.common_trap: Picking rhamnose, which is an exception in the opposite direction.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following does NOT reduce Fehling's solution or Tollens' reagent?

solution.key_concept: A disaccharide is reducing only if a free hemiacetal or hemiketal group remains.
steps: In sucrose, C1 of glucose and C2 of fructose are both locked in the glycosidic bond.
Maltose and lactose keep a free hemiacetal group, and all monosaccharides, including fructose, are reducing.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Sucrose
solution.why_not_others: Maltose and lactose are reducing disaccharides. Fructose is a monosaccharide, so it is reducing.
solution.common_trap: Assuming fructose is non-reducing because it is a ketose.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: I
list_II.text: Aldotriose

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Ketohexose

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Aldopentose

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Aldohexose

solution.key_concept: Classify each sugar by its carbonyl type and its number of carbons.
steps: Glucose is an aldohexose (IV).
Fructose is a ketohexose (II).
Ribose is an aldopentose (III).
Glyceraldehyde is an aldotriose (I).
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 swaps glucose and fructose between aldose and ketose. Options 2 and 3 assign the wrong carbon counts to ribose and glyceraldehyde.
solution.common_trap: Interchanging the aldose and ketose labels of glucose and fructose.
solution.time_saving_tip: Fixing glucose as IV and fructose as II leaves only options 2 and 4; ribose (C5) then settles the answer.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the classification and configuration of carbohydrates are correct?

statements.A: Oligosaccharides give 2 to 10 monosaccharide units on hydrolysis.
statements.B: D or L configuration of a sugar is assigned relative to glyceraldehyde.
statements.D: In a D-sugar, the $-OH$ on the lowest asymmetric carbon points to the right in the Fischer projection.
statements.E: Polysaccharides such as starch and cellulose are sweet, water-soluble sugars.

solution.key_concept: D/L describes configuration, not the sign of optical rotation, and polysaccharides are non-sugars.
steps: Statements A, B and D are correct.
Statement C is false: fructose is a D-sugar yet laevorotatory.
Statement E is false: polysaccharides are not sweet and are generally insoluble.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A, B and D only
solution.why_not_others: Options 1 and 4 include the false statement C. Option 2 includes the false statement E and leaves out the correct statement A.
solution.common_trap: Equating D with (+) and L with (-).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Prolonged heating of glucose with $HI$ gives

solution.key_concept: Reduction of glucose by $HI$ shows that its six carbon atoms form a straight chain.
steps: $CHO(CHOH)_4CH_2OH \xrightarrow{HI,\ \Delta} CH_3(CH_2)_4CH_3$
The product, n-hexane, proves the straight six-carbon chain.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): n-Hexane
solution.why_not_others: Gluconic acid is formed with bromine water. Saccharic acid is formed with $HNO_3$. The pentaacetate is formed by acetylation.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the reagent for each product.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which reaction of glucose establishes the presence of a primary alcohol group in it?
options: Oxidation with bromine water to gluconic acid
Oxidation with nitric acid to saccharic acid
Reaction with $HCN$ to form a cyanohydrin

solution.key_concept: $HNO_3$ oxidises both the $-CHO$ group and the $-CH_2OH$ group of glucose to $-COOH$.
steps: $CHO(CHOH)_4CH_2OH \xrightarrow{HNO_3} COOH(CHOH)_4COOH$ (saccharic acid)
Since the terminal $-CH_2OH$ becomes $-COOH$, a primary alcohol group must be present.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Oxidation with nitric acid to saccharic acid
solution.why_not_others: Bromine water proves an aldehyde group. The pentaacetate proves five $-OH$ groups. Cyanohydrin formation proves a carbonyl group.
solution.common_trap: Choosing gluconic acid, which proves only the aldehyde group.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following facts about glucose CANNOT be explained by its open-chain structure?
options: It gives n-hexane on prolonged heating with $HI$
It does not form an adduct with $NaHSO_3$
It forms a pentaacetate on acetylation

solution.key_concept: Some properties of glucose require its cyclic hemiacetal (pyranose) structure.
steps: A free $-CHO$ group should form a $NaHSO_3$ adduct and give Schiff's test, but glucose does neither.
This is explained by the cyclic hemiacetal formed between the C5 $-OH$ and the $-CHO$ group.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): It does not form an adduct with $NaHSO_3$
solution.why_not_others: Oxime formation, n-hexane formation and pentaacetate formation are all consistent with the open-chain structure; they are the evidence for it.
solution.common_trap: Choosing a reaction that actually supports the open-chain structure.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.R: Only aldoses, and not ketoses, are reducing sugars.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: All monosaccharides, both aldoses and ketoses, are reducing sugars.
steps: Fructose is a monosaccharide, so it reduces Tollens' reagent; A is true.
Ketoses are also reducing sugars, so R is false.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A is true but R is false
solution.why_not_others: R is false, which rules out options 1, 2 and 4.
solution.common_trap: Believing ketoses cannot reduce Tollens' reagent.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Alpha- and beta-D-glucose are anomers that differ only in configuration at C1; the alpha form melts at 419 K and the beta form at 423 K.
statements.II: Fructose forms a five-membered furanose ring through its C5 $-OH$, whereas glucose forms a six-membered pyranose ring.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: These are the cyclic structures of glucose and fructose and the properties of the glucose anomers.
steps: The anomers differ only at C1, the anomeric carbon, and melt at 419 K (alpha) and 423 K (beta); Statement I is correct.
Fructose forms a furanose ring and glucose a pyranose ring; Statement II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Both statements match the facts, so every option that marks one of them incorrect is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the melting points or the ring sizes.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: Constituent monosaccharides of sucrose, lactose and maltose
questions.question: Hydrolysis of lactose (milk sugar) gives

solution.key_concept: Lactose is made of beta-D-galactose and beta-D-glucose linked C1 to C4.
steps: Hydrolysis breaks the glycosidic linkage.
The products are D-galactose and D-glucose.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): D-galactose and D-glucose
solution.why_not_others: Two units of D-glucose come from maltose. D-glucose and D-fructose come from sucrose. Fructose is not present in lactose.
solution.common_trap: Confusing lactose with maltose.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: Constituent monosaccharides of sucrose, lactose and maltose
questions.question: In sucrose, the glycosidic linkage joins
options: C1 of alpha-D-glucose and C4 of beta-D-fructose
C1 of alpha-D-glucose and C2 of beta-D-fructose
C1 of one alpha-D-glucose and C4 of another alpha-D-glucose
C2 of alpha-D-glucose and C1 of beta-D-fructose

solution.key_concept: In sucrose the reducing groups of both units are used up in the glycosidic bond.
steps: The glucose reducing carbon is C1 and the fructose reducing carbon is C2.
The C1 to C2 linkage leaves no free hemiacetal group, so sucrose is non-reducing.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): C1 of alpha-D-glucose and C2 of beta-D-fructose
solution.why_not_others: A C1 to C4 link between two glucose units describes maltose. The other options give wrong carbon positions.
solution.common_trap: Assuming the C1 to C4 pattern of maltose and lactose also applies to sucrose.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: Constituent monosaccharides of sucrose, lactose and maltose
questions.question: The acid- or invertase-catalysed hydrolysis of sucrose is called inversion because
options: laevorotatory sucrose gives a dextrorotatory product mixture
fructose is converted into glucose during the reaction
dextrorotatory sucrose gives a laevorotatory mixture, as the rotation of fructose ($-92.4^\circ$) outweighs that of glucose ($+52.5^\circ$)
the D-configuration of the sugars changes to the L-configuration

solution.key_concept: Inversion is the change in the sign of optical rotation when sucrose is hydrolysed.
steps: Sucrose is dextrorotatory.
Its hydrolysis gives glucose ($+52.5^\circ$) and fructose ($-92.4^\circ$).
The fructose term is larger in magnitude, so the net rotation becomes negative and the product is invert sugar.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): dextrorotatory sucrose gives a laevorotatory mixture, as the rotation of fructose ($-92.4^\circ$) outweighs that of glucose ($+52.5^\circ$)
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 reverses the signs. No interconversion of fructose and glucose occurs. The configuration remains D; only the sign of rotation changes.
solution.common_trap: Thinking inversion means a change of D to L configuration.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: Constituent monosaccharides of sucrose, lactose and maltose
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: I
list_II.text: Alpha-D-glucose + alpha-D-glucose, linked C1 to C4

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Beta-D-galactose + beta-D-glucose, linked C1 to C4

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Alpha-D-glucose + beta-D-fructose, linked C1 to C2

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Laevorotatory mixture of D-glucose and D-fructose

solution.key_concept: Each disaccharide has its own constituent units and linkage.
steps: Sucrose matches III and maltose matches I.
Lactose matches II.
Invert sugar, the product of hydrolysing sucrose, matches IV.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 confuses sucrose with its hydrolysis product. Option 3 swaps maltose and lactose. Option 4 swaps sucrose and maltose.
solution.common_trap: Matching sucrose to invert sugar.
solution.time_saving_tip: Galactose fixes lactose as II, which removes options 3 and 1 is removed by D.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: Constituent monosaccharides of sucrose, lactose and maltose
questions.question: Which of the following statements about sucrose, maltose and lactose are correct?

statements.A: Maltose is a reducing sugar because its second glucose unit retains a free hemiacetal group.
statements.B: Sucrose is non-reducing because the reducing groups of both its units are used up in the glycosidic bond.
statements.C: Lactose is non-reducing because it contains galactose.
statements.D: The enzyme maltase hydrolyses maltose into D-glucose and D-fructose.
statements.E: Among these three disaccharides, galactose is present only in lactose.

solution.key_concept: Reducing behaviour depends on whether a free hemiacetal group remains, and each disaccharide has fixed constituents.
steps: Statements A and B are correct.
Statement C is false: lactose keeps a free hemiacetal group, so it is reducing.
Statement D is false: maltase gives 2 D-glucose units.
Statement E is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A, B and E only
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 leaves out the correct statement E. Option 2 includes the false statement C. Option 3 includes the false statement D.
solution.common_trap: Linking galactose with non-reducing behaviour.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: Alpha-amino acids, peptide bond and polypeptides
questions.question: Which one of the following naturally occurring alpha-amino acids is optically inactive?

solution.key_concept: All natural alpha-amino acids except glycine are optically active.
steps: The general formula of an alpha-amino acid is $R-CH(NH_2)-COOH$.
In glycine $R = H$, so the alpha carbon carries two identical H atoms and is not chiral.
Alanine ($R = CH_3$), valine and leucine have a chiral alpha carbon and are optically active.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Glycine
solution.why_not_others: Alanine, valine and leucine each have four different groups on the alpha carbon, so they are optically active.
solution.common_trap: Choosing alanine because it is the next simplest amino acid. Its $CH_3$ group still makes the alpha carbon chiral.
solution.time_saving_tip: Remember that glycine is the only natural alpha-amino acid that is not optically active.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: Alpha-amino acids, peptide bond and polypeptides
questions.question: The correct structure of the dipeptide glycylalanine (Gly-Ala) is

solution.key_concept: A peptide bond is the amide link $-CO-NH-$ formed between the $-COOH$ of one amino acid and the $-NH_2$ of the next, with loss of water.
steps: In Gly-Ala, glycine is the residue with the free $-NH_2$ group and alanine is the residue with the free $-COOH$ group.
The $-COOH$ of glycine joins the $-NH_2$ of alanine to form $-CO-NH-$.
This gives $H_2N-CH_2-CO-NH-CH(CH_3)-COOH$.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): $H_2N-CH_2-CO-NH-CH(CH_3)-COOH$
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) is Ala-Gly, with the order reversed. Option (2) contains an ester link instead of an amide link. In option (3), the carboxyl group of alanine has formed the amide with the amino group of glycine, so the free $-NH_2$ is on alanine and the free $-COOH$ is on glycine. That is again Ala-Gly, not Gly-Ala.
solution.common_trap: Ignoring the sequence and accepting Ala-Gly as Gly-Ala.
solution.time_saving_tip: Check which residue has the free $NH_2$. That residue is named first.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: Alpha-amino acids, peptide bond and polypeptides
questions.question: Alpha-amino acids are amphoteric, crystalline solids with high melting points. This is mainly because
options: most of them have the L-configuration
their $-NH_2$ and $-COOH$ groups are attached to different carbon atoms

solution.key_concept: Zwitterion formation explains the amphoteric nature and high melting points of amino acids.
steps: The acidic $-COOH$ group transfers a proton to the basic $-NH_2$ group: $R-CH(NH_2)-COOH \rightleftharpoons R-CH(NH_3^+)-COO^-$.
The dipolar ion has both an acidic part ($-NH_3^+$) and a basic part ($-COO^-$), so the compound is amphoteric.
Its ionic character makes amino acids crystalline solids with high melting points.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): they exist as dipolar ions, $H_3N^+-CHR-COO^-$
solution.why_not_others: Optical activity and L-configuration describe stereochemistry and do not explain these properties. In alpha-amino acids both groups are on the same alpha carbon, so option (4) is factually wrong.
solution.common_trap: Linking physical properties to optical activity instead of to ionic character.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: Alpha-amino acids, peptide bond and polypeptides
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Glycine is the only naturally occurring alpha-amino acid that is optically inactive.
statements.R: In glycine the side chain R is a hydrogen atom, so its alpha carbon carries two identical hydrogen atoms and is not chiral.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Optical activity requires a chiral alpha carbon. Glycine ($R = H$) does not have one.
steps: All natural alpha-amino acids except glycine are optically active, so A is true.
Glycine is $H_2N-CH_2-COOH$; its alpha carbon has two H atoms, so R is true.
A carbon with two identical groups is not chiral, so R directly explains A.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: R gives the structural reason for A, so options (2), (3) and (4) are ruled out.
solution.common_trap: Thinking R is only a description of glycine and not the explanation of its optical inactivity.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: Alpha-amino acids, peptide bond and polypeptides
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: A peptide formed by linking eleven alpha-amino acid molecules is classified as a polypeptide.
statements.II: A polypeptide containing more than about 100 amino acid residues and having a molecular mass above 10000 u is called a protein.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Peptides are classified by the number of amino acid units they contain.
steps: Two amino acids form a dipeptide. More than ten amino acids form a polypeptide.
Eleven is more than ten, so Statement I is correct.
A polypeptide with more than about 100 residues and molecular mass above 10000 u is a protein, so Statement II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Both statements agree with the definitions, so no option that marks either statement as incorrect can be right.
solution.common_trap: Thinking a polypeptide needs about 100 residues. That figure is the threshold for a protein, not for a polypeptide.
solution.time_saving_tip: Remember the cut-offs: more than 10 residues for a polypeptide; more than about 100 residues and above 10000 u for a protein.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: Protein structure: primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary
questions.question: The primary structure of a protein refers to
options: the twisting of the chain into a helix
the sequence of amino acids in the polypeptide chain
the spatial arrangement of two or more polypeptide subunits
the overall folding of the chain into a globular shape

solution.key_concept: The primary structure is the amino acid sequence, held by peptide bonds.
steps: The four levels are primary (sequence), secondary (helix or sheet), tertiary (overall folding) and quaternary (arrangement of subunits).
The sequence of amino acids is the primary structure.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): the sequence of amino acids in the polypeptide chain
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) describes secondary structure, option (3) quaternary structure and option (4) tertiary structure.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the overall folded shape with the primary structure.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: Protein structure: primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the alpha-helix structure of proteins?
options: A right-handed screw held by intramolecular hydrogen bonds between the $-NH$ of one residue and the $>C=O$ of an adjacent turn
A left-handed screw held by intramolecular hydrogen bonds between the $-NH$ and $>C=O$ groups
A right-handed screw held by intermolecular hydrogen bonds between neighbouring chains
A left-handed screw held mainly by disulphide linkages

solution.key_concept: The alpha-helix is right-handed and is stabilised by intramolecular hydrogen bonds.
steps: In the alpha-helix, the polypeptide chain twists into a right-handed screw.
The $-NH$ of one residue hydrogen-bonds to the $>C=O$ of an adjacent turn of the same chain, so the bonds are intramolecular.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): A right-handed screw held by intramolecular hydrogen bonds between the $-NH$ of one residue and the $>C=O$ of an adjacent turn
solution.why_not_others: Options (2) and (4) wrongly make the helix left-handed. Option (3) describes the intermolecular hydrogen bonding of the beta-pleated sheet.
solution.common_trap: Calling the alpha-helix left-handed.
solution.time_saving_tip: Pair the terms: helix goes with intramolecular hydrogen bonds; sheet goes with intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: Protein structure: primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary
questions.question: Which statement about the quaternary structure of proteins is correct?
options: It exists only in proteins made of two or more polypeptide subunits, as in haemoglobin, which has four subunits
Every biologically active protein must possess a quaternary structure
It refers to the sequence of amino acids joined by peptide bonds
It is the side-by-side arrangement of stretched chains held by intermolecular hydrogen bonds

solution.key_concept: Quaternary structure is the spatial arrangement of two or more polypeptide subunits.
steps: Quaternary structure requires at least two subunits; haemoglobin has four.
Proteins with only tertiary structure can also be fully biologically active, so quaternary structure is not essential for activity.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): It exists only in proteins made of two or more polypeptide subunits, as in haemoglobin, which has four subunits
solution.why_not_others: Option (2) is false because single-chain proteins can be fully active. Option (3) describes primary structure. Option (4) describes the beta-pleated sheet.
solution.common_trap: Assuming every biologically active protein needs a quaternary structure.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: Protein structure: primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: I
list_II.text: Chains stretched almost to maximum extension, laid side by side and held by intermolecular hydrogen bonds

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Sequence of amino acids linked by peptide bonds

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Spatial arrangement of two or more polypeptide subunits

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Right-handed coil stabilised by intramolecular hydrogen bonds

solution.key_concept: Each level of protein structure has a characteristic feature.
steps: Primary structure is the amino acid sequence: A-II.
Alpha-helix is a right-handed coil with intramolecular hydrogen bonds: B-IV.
Beta-pleated sheet has side-by-side chains with intermolecular hydrogen bonds: C-I.
Quaternary structure is the arrangement of subunits: D-III.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) swaps the helix and the sheet. Option (3) swaps the primary and quaternary structures. Option (4) swaps the sheet and the quaternary structure.
solution.common_trap: Interchanging intramolecular hydrogen bonding (helix) with intermolecular hydrogen bonding (sheet).
solution.time_saving_tip: Once A-II and B-IV are fixed, only option (2) remains.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: Protein structure: primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary
questions.question: Which of the following statements about protein structure are correct?

statements.A: A change of even a single amino acid in the sequence can alter the function of a protein.
statements.B: Tertiary structure is stabilised by hydrogen bonds, disulphide linkages, van der Waals forces and electrostatic attractions.
statements.C: A protein that has only a tertiary structure cannot be biologically active.
statements.D: In the beta-pleated sheet, polypeptide chains are stretched almost to maximum extension.
statements.E: Haemoglobin is made up of two polypeptide subunits.

options: A, B, C and D only

solution.key_concept: These statements test the features of each level of protein structure.
steps: A is true: the primary structure determines function.
B is true: these four forces stabilise tertiary structure.
C is false: proteins with only tertiary structure can be fully biologically active.
D is true: in the sheet, chains are nearly fully extended and laid side by side.
E is false: haemoglobin has four subunits.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): A, B and D only
solution.why_not_others: Option (2) includes C, option (3) includes E, and option (4) includes both C and E. Each of these contains a false statement.
solution.common_trap: Believing that quaternary structure is required for biological activity, or miscounting the subunits in haemoglobin.
solution.time_saving_tip: Rejecting C and E removes every option except (1).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: When a protein is denatured, which level of its structure remains intact?

solution.key_concept: Denaturation destroys secondary and tertiary structure but not the peptide bonds.
steps: Heat or a change in pH disturbs the hydrogen bonds, so helices uncoil and globules unfold.
Peptide bonds are not broken, so the amino acid sequence (primary structure) is retained.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Primary structure
solution.why_not_others: Secondary and tertiary structures are exactly the levels destroyed during denaturation.
solution.common_trap: Thinking that denaturation breaks peptide bonds.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Curdling of milk is an example of protein denaturation. It is caused by
options: breaking of peptide bonds in milk proteins by bacterial enzymes
destruction of the primary structure of milk proteins by heat
a rise in pH due to bases released by bacteria
a change in pH due to lactic acid produced by bacteria

solution.key_concept: A change in pH is a chemical cause of denaturation.
steps: Bacteria in milk produce lactic acid.
The acid changes the pH, which disturbs the hydrogen bonds in the milk proteins.
The proteins lose their secondary and tertiary structure, and the milk curdles.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): a change in pH due to lactic acid produced by bacteria
solution.why_not_others: Options (1) and (2) involve breaking peptide bonds or the primary structure, which does not happen in denaturation. Option (3) is wrong because lactic acid lowers the pH; it does not raise it.
solution.common_trap: Assuming curdling involves breaking peptide bonds.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: When a protein is denatured by heat or by a change in pH, the interactions mainly disturbed are

solution.key_concept: Denaturation acts by disturbing hydrogen bonds.
steps: Heat or a change in pH disturbs the hydrogen bonds.
As a result, globules unfold, helices uncoil and biological activity is lost.
Covalent peptide bonds remain unbroken.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): hydrogen bonds
solution.why_not_others: Peptide bonds and backbone C-C bonds remain intact during denaturation. Glycosidic linkages occur in carbohydrates, not in proteins.
solution.common_trap: Choosing peptide bonds because the protein loses its activity.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Egg white coagulated by boiling still contains the same sequence of amino acids as the native egg-white protein.
statements.R: Denaturation destroys the secondary and tertiary structures of a protein but does not break its peptide bonds.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: The primary structure survives denaturation.
steps: Boiling egg white is a case of denaturation.
Because peptide bonds are not broken, the amino acid sequence is unchanged, so A is true.
R is true and is the very reason the sequence is unchanged, so R explains A.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are true and R directly accounts for A, so options (2), (3) and (4) are ruled out.
solution.common_trap: Assuming that boiling breaks the protein down into fragments.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: A denatured protein retains its biological activity because its primary structure remains unchanged.
statements.II: During denaturation, the globules of a protein unfold and its helices uncoil.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Denaturation causes loss of biological activity even though the primary structure is retained.
steps: The primary structure is retained, but the loss of secondary and tertiary structure makes the protein lose its biological activity. Statement I is therefore incorrect.
When hydrogen bonds are disturbed, globules unfold and helices uncoil, so Statement II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
solution.why_not_others: Statement I contradicts the loss of activity on denaturation, and Statement II matches the notes. No other option fits this combination.
solution.common_trap: Concluding that an intact primary structure keeps the protein active.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The enzyme that converts maltose into glucose is

solution.key_concept: Enzymes are highly specific for their substrate.
steps: Maltase acts specifically on maltose, converting it to glucose.
Invertase (sucrase) hydrolyses sucrose instead.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): maltase
solution.why_not_others: Invertase acts on sucrose. Lactase and amylase act on other substrates, not on maltose.
solution.common_trap: Confusing invertase with maltase.
solution.time_saving_tip: The name of the enzyme usually reflects its substrate: malt-ase acts on maltose.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The activation energy for the acid hydrolysis of sucrose is about 6.22 kJ mol$^{-1}$. With the enzyme sucrase it is about 2.15 kJ mol$^{-1}$. By how much does the enzyme lower the activation energy?

solution.key_concept: Enzymes act by lowering the activation energy.
steps: Decrease = $4.07$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): 4.07 kJ mol$^{-1}$
solution.why_not_others: 8.37 comes from adding the two values. 2.89 is their ratio ($6.22/2.15$), which is a pure number and not an energy. 6.22 is simply the uncatalysed value.
solution.common_trap: Dividing the two values instead of subtracting them.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: I
list_II.text: Region where the substrate binds to form the enzyme-substrate complex

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Catalyses oxidation of one substrate with simultaneous reduction of another

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Hydrolyses sucrose

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Converts maltose into glucose

solution.key_concept: This question tests enzyme names, their specificity and the mechanism of action.
steps: Maltase converts maltose to glucose: A-IV.
Invertase hydrolyses sucrose: B-III.
Oxidoreductases catalyse coupled oxidation and reduction: C-II.
The substrate binds at the active site to form the ES complex: D-I.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) swaps maltase and invertase. Option (2) swaps the oxidoreductase and the active site. Option (3) swaps invertase and the oxidoreductase.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the substrates of maltase and invertase.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about enzymes are correct?

statements.B: Enzymes are highly specific for their substrate and for the reaction they catalyse.
statements.C: Enzyme action can be represented as $E + S \rightleftharpoons ES \rightarrow E + P$, with the complex formed at the active site.
statements.D: Enzymes work best at high temperatures and at extreme pH.
statements.E: Enzymes change the equilibrium constant of the reactions they catalyse.

options: A, B, C and E only

solution.key_concept: These statements test the nature, specificity, mechanism and operating conditions of enzymes.
steps: A is true: most enzymes are globular proteins.
B is true: enzymes are highly specific.
C is true: this is the enzyme-substrate complex mechanism.
D is false: enzymes work under mild conditions, at an optimum temperature and pH.
E is false: enzymes lower the activation energy without changing the equilibrium.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A, B and C only
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) leaves out the true statement C. Option (2) includes the false statement E. Option (4) includes the false statement D and leaves out A.
solution.common_trap: Thinking that a catalyst alters the equilibrium constant.
solution.time_saving_tip: Rejecting D and E leaves A, B and C.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Deficiency of which vitamin causes scurvy?

solution.key_concept: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) deficiency causes scurvy.
steps: Scurvy is the deficiency disease of vitamin C.
Vitamin C sources are citrus fruits, amla and green leafy vegetables.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Vitamin C
solution.why_not_others: Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness and xerophthalmia. Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets. Vitamin $B_1$ deficiency causes beri beri.
solution.common_trap: Confusing scurvy with rickets, which is caused by vitamin D deficiency.
solution.time_saving_tip: Pair C with citrus and scurvy.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following vitamins is water-soluble but is still stored in the liver?

solution.key_concept: Water-soluble vitamins are normally excreted in urine. Vitamin $B_{12}$ is the exception because it is stored in the liver.
steps: Water-soluble vitamins (the B group and C) are excreted in urine and must be supplied regularly.
Vitamin $B_{12}$ is water-soluble but is stored in the liver.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Vitamin $B_{12}$
solution.why_not_others: Vitamins C and $B_1$ are water-soluble and are excreted in urine, so they are not stored. Vitamin H (biotin) is soluble in neither water nor fat.
solution.common_trap: Assuming all water-soluble vitamins behave alike and none is stored.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following vitamin–deficiency disease pairs is correctly matched?

solution.key_concept: Each vitamin has its own specific deficiency disease.
steps: $B_1$ deficiency causes beri beri, $B_2$ causes cheilosis and $B_6$ causes convulsions.
$B_{12}$ deficiency causes pernicious anaemia.
E deficiency causes fragile RBCs, and K deficiency causes increased blood clotting time.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Vitamin $B_6$ – convulsions
solution.why_not_others: Cheilosis is due to $B_2$, not $B_1$. Pernicious anaemia is due to $B_{12}$, not $B_2$. Fragile RBCs are due to vitamin E, not K.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the B-vitamin numbers ($B_1$, $B_2$, $B_6$, $B_{12}$) with their diseases.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Vitamin C must be supplied regularly in the diet.
statements.R: Vitamin C is water-soluble and is excreted in urine, so it is not stored in the body.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Water-soluble vitamins are excreted in urine and so must be supplied regularly.
steps: Vitamin C is a water-soluble vitamin.
Water-soluble vitamins are excreted in urine and cannot be stored, so they must be taken regularly.
R is therefore the reason A is true.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are true, and the lack of storage directly explains the need for regular intake.
solution.common_trap: Applying the $B_{12}$ exception to vitamin C. Only $B_{12}$ is stored in the liver.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Vitamins A, D, E and K are stored in the liver and adipose tissue.
statements.II: Vitamin H (biotin) is water-soluble and therefore must be supplied regularly in the diet.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Fat-soluble vitamins are stored in the body. Biotin is soluble in neither water nor fat.
steps: A, D, E and K are fat-soluble and are stored in the liver and adipose tissue, so Statement I is correct.
Vitamin H (biotin) is soluble in neither water nor fat, so Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement II wrongly classifies biotin as water-soluble, so any option calling Statement II correct is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Grouping biotin with the B-group water-soluble vitamins.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: Nucleic acids: chemical constitution of DNA and RNA
questions.question: Which nitrogenous base is present in RNA but not in DNA?

solution.key_concept: In RNA, uracil replaces thymine.
steps: DNA bases are A, G, C and T.
RNA bases are A, G, C and U, so uracil is found only in RNA.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Uracil
solution.why_not_others: Adenine and cytosine occur in both DNA and RNA. Thymine occurs only in DNA.
solution.common_trap: Choosing thymine, which is the DNA-only base.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: Nucleic acids: chemical constitution of DNA and RNA
questions.question: A nucleotide differs from the corresponding nucleoside in having
options: a nitrogenous base attached at C1' of the sugar
a phosphoric acid group esterified at C1' of the sugar
a phosphoric acid group esterified at C5' of the sugar
an additional hydroxyl group at C2' of the sugar

solution.key_concept: Nucleoside = base + sugar. Nucleotide = nucleoside + phosphate esterified at C5'.
steps: A nucleoside is a base attached at C1' of the pentose sugar.
A nucleotide is formed when phosphoric acid is esterified at C5' of the nucleoside.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): a phosphoric acid group esterified at C5' of the sugar
solution.why_not_others: The base at C1' is present in both, so it is not a difference. C1' carries the base, not the phosphate. A C2' hydroxyl distinguishes ribose from deoxyribose, not a nucleotide from a nucleoside.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up nucleoside and nucleotide, or misplacing the phosphate position.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: Nucleic acids: chemical constitution of DNA and RNA
questions.question: A sample of double-stranded DNA contains 20% adenine. What is the percentage of guanine in it?

solution.key_concept: In double-stranded DNA, $[A] = [T]$ and $[G] = [C]$.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): 30%
solution.why_not_others: 20% wrongly assumes G equals A. 60% is the total of G + C. 40% is the total of A + T.
solution.common_trap: Forgetting to divide G + C equally between G and C.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: Nucleic acids: chemical constitution of DNA and RNA
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_I.label: C
list_I.text: Number of hydrogen bonds in a G–C base pair

list_I.label: D
list_I.text: Number of hydrogen bonds in an A–T base pair

list_II.label: I
list_II.text: $\beta$-D-ribose

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Three

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: $\beta$-D-2-deoxyribose

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Two

solution.key_concept: DNA contains 2-deoxyribose and RNA contains ribose. G≡C pairs by three H-bonds and A=T by two.
steps: DNA sugar is $\beta$-D-2-deoxyribose: A-III.
RNA sugar is $\beta$-D-ribose: B-I.
G pairs with C through three hydrogen bonds: C-II.
A pairs with T through two hydrogen bonds: D-IV.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
solution.why_not_others: Options (1) and (3) swap the two sugars. Options (2) and (3) swap the hydrogen-bond numbers.
solution.common_trap: Reversing the hydrogen-bond counts of the G–C and A–T pairs.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.topic: Nucleic acids: chemical constitution of DNA and RNA
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the constitution of nucleic acids are correct?

statements.A: Adenine and guanine are purine bases.
statements.B: Thymine and uracil are purine bases.
statements.C: Nucleotides are joined by phosphodiester linkages between C5' and C3' of adjacent sugar units.
statements.E: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine through three hydrogen bonds.

solution.key_concept: Purines are A and G, and pyrimidines are C, T and U. The backbone uses 5'-3' phosphodiester links. A=T pairs by two H-bonds.
steps: A is correct: adenine and guanine are purines.
B is incorrect: thymine and uracil are pyrimidines.
C is correct: adjacent sugars are joined by 5'-3' phosphodiester bonds.
D is correct: deoxyribose has no $-OH$ at C2'.
E is incorrect: A–T pairing involves two hydrogen bonds, not three.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A, C and D only
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) omits the correct statement D. Option (2) includes the false statement B. Option (3) includes the false statement E.
solution.common_trap: Calling thymine and uracil purines, or giving A–T three hydrogen bonds.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which type of nucleic acid brings specific amino acids to the site of protein synthesis?

solution.key_concept: tRNA is the transfer RNA that carries specific amino acids.
steps: mRNA carries the message from DNA.
tRNA brings specific amino acids.
rRNA forms part of the ribosomes.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): tRNA
solution.why_not_others: mRNA carries the code. rRNA is a structural part of ribosomes. DNA directs synthesis but does not carry amino acids.
solution.common_trap: Confusing mRNA (message) with tRNA (amino acid carrier).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the role of nucleic acids in protein synthesis is correct?
options: DNA itself carries out the actual synthesis of proteins in the cell.
DNA directs protein synthesis, but RNA molecules carry out the actual synthesis.
mRNA forms part of the ribosomes where proteins are assembled.
rRNA carries the message from DNA to the site of protein synthesis.

solution.key_concept: DNA directs protein synthesis, while RNA molecules perform it.
steps: DNA holds the information, and RNA molecules carry out the synthesis.
mRNA carries the message, tRNA brings amino acids and rRNA forms ribosomes.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): DNA directs protein synthesis, but RNA molecules carry out the actual synthesis.
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) is wrong because RNA, not DNA, does the actual synthesis. Options (3) and (4) swap the roles of mRNA and rRNA.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the functions of mRNA and rRNA.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: DNA fingerprinting, used in forensics and paternity testing, is based on the fact that
options: the DNA sequence is identical in all human beings
the DNA sequence of every person is unique
DNA does not replicate before cell division
information flows from protein to DNA

solution.key_concept: Each individual's DNA sequence is unique, which allows identification.
steps: DNA fingerprinting compares DNA sequences.
Because each person's DNA sequence is unique, it can identify individuals.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): the DNA sequence of every person is unique
solution.why_not_others: If the DNA sequence were identical in all humans, no individual could be identified. DNA does replicate before cell division. Information flows from DNA to RNA to protein, not the reverse.
solution.common_trap: Thinking fingerprinting relies on similarity rather than uniqueness.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: DNA replicates before a cell divides.
statements.R: Replication of DNA gives each daughter cell only half of the genetic information of the parent cell.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: DNA replicates before cell division so that each daughter cell gets an identical, complete copy.
steps: A is true: DNA replicates before cell division.
R is false: each daughter cell receives an identical copy, not half the information.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A is true but R is false
solution.why_not_others: R is false, so options (1) and (2) are ruled out. A is true, so option (4) is ruled out.
solution.common_trap: Believing replication splits the information between daughter cells.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: The genetic code carried by DNA keeps the identity of different species over millions of years.
statements.II: rRNA forms part of the ribosomes, where proteins are assembled.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: DNA is the basis of heredity, and rRNA is a structural component of ribosomes.
steps: Statement I is correct: DNA's genetic code maintains species identity over millions of years.
Statement II is correct: rRNA forms part of the ribosomes, the site of protein assembly.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Both statements match the stated functions, so any option calling either one incorrect is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Thinking mRNA, rather than rRNA, forms the ribosomes.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is a polypeptide hormone?

solution.key_concept: Hormones are classified as steroids, polypeptides or amino acid derivatives.
steps: Polypeptide hormones include insulin and endorphins.
Thyroxine and epinephrine are amino acid derivatives, and testosterone is a steroid.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Insulin
solution.why_not_others: Thyroxine and epinephrine are amino acid derivatives. Testosterone is a steroid.
solution.common_trap: Assuming thyroxine is a polypeptide because it comes from an amino acid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Thyroxine, produced in the thyroid gland, is an iodinated derivative of which amino acid?

solution.key_concept: Thyroxine is an iodinated derivative of tyrosine.
steps: Thyroxine is classed as an amino acid derivative hormone.
It is derived from tyrosine by iodination.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Tyrosine
solution.why_not_others: Glycine, tryptophan and phenylalanine are not the parent amino acid of thyroxine.
solution.common_trap: Choosing phenylalanine because of its structural similarity to tyrosine.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Deficiency of the hormones of the adrenal cortex results in

solution.key_concept: Deficiency of adrenal cortex hormones causes Addison's disease.
steps: The adrenal cortex secretes glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids.
Their deficiency causes Addison's disease.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Addison's disease
solution.why_not_others: Goitre is caused by iodine deficiency. Hypothyroidism is caused by too little thyroxine. Hyperthyroidism is caused by excess thyroxine.
solution.common_trap: Attributing thyroid disorders to the adrenal gland.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: I
list_II.text: Control excretion of water and salt by the kidney

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Prepares the uterus for implantation

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Keep blood glucose within a narrow range

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Control carbohydrate metabolism and inflammation

solution.key_concept: Each hormone or hormone group regulates a specific function.
steps: Glucocorticoids control carbohydrate metabolism and inflammation: A-IV.
Mineralocorticoids control water and salt excretion by the kidney: B-I.
Insulin and glucagon regulate blood glucose: C-III.
Progesterone prepares the uterus for implantation: D-II.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) swaps the glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid functions. Option (2) swaps C and D. Option (4) gives the blood glucose role to glucocorticoids.
solution.common_trap: Confusing glucocorticoids with mineralocorticoids.
solution.time_saving_tip: Mineralo- means minerals (salt and water); gluco- means carbohydrate.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about hormones are correct?

statements.A: Estrogens and androgens are steroid hormones.
statements.B: Endorphins are amino acid derivative hormones.
statements.C: Epinephrine and norepinephrine mediate responses to external stimuli.
statements.D: Excess thyroxine causes hypothyroidism, marked by lethargy and obesity.
statements.E: Iodine deficiency causes enlargement of the thyroid gland, called goitre.

solution.key_concept: Hormone classes and thyroid disorders.
steps: A is correct: estrogens and androgens are steroids.
B is incorrect: endorphins are polypeptides.
C is correct: epinephrine and norepinephrine mediate responses to external stimuli.
D is incorrect: too little thyroxine causes hypothyroidism, while excess causes hyperthyroidism.
E is correct: iodine deficiency causes goitre.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): A, C and E only
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) includes the false statement B. Options (3) and (4) include the false statement D.
solution.common_trap: Linking hypothyroidism to excess thyroxine, or classifying endorphins as amino acid derivatives.
